environment.description: Same Ktor service deployed behind AWS API Gateway (HTTP API type) with a usage plan attached. The usage plan enforces a throttle of 2 requests per second with a burst of 3, scoped to the /api/v2/documents/upload resource specifically. Additionally, the API Gateway stage has a default route-level throttle of 5 rps. The API Gateway integration timeout is set to 10 seconds. A CloudFront distribution sits in front with a custom origin request policy that strips multipart bodies exceeding 1MB at the edge (via CloudFront Function 'validate-upload-size' which returns 413 for Content-Length > 1048576). The /files/* path is NOT routed through API Gateway — it is served from an S3 bucket via CloudFront with a restrictive bucket policy that sets Content-Disposition: attachment on all objects and Content-Type: application/octet-stream regardless of extension, enforced by a Lambda@Edge origin-response function. The S3 bucket has a lifecycle rule deleting objects after 24 hours.

config.api_gateway: AWS HTTP API with usage plan: 2 rps / burst 3 on upload endpoint
config.file_serving: S3 + CloudFront with Lambda@Edge forcing Content-Disposition: attachment and Content-Type: application/octet-stream
config.network: Ktor service in private subnet, only reachable via API Gateway VPC link
